newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief wants action against wider African war.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief wants action against wider African war.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Friday called for an international conference to prevent warfare in Zaire from spreading throughout the central African region.

But first he said a "provisional solution" had to be found to end the fighting in eastern Zaire and he planned to send a new mediator with a team of assistants to help quell the emergency. He did not name the new mediator.
In answer to questions during Security Council consultations, Boutros-Ghali said he would welcome military observers if the council wanted to send them.

Fighting is raging in eastern Zaire between Rwandan Tutsis, who have lived in the region since the 18th century, and the Zairean army. The United Nations fears the fighting could spread further and Tutsi-dominated armies in neighbouring Burundi and Rwanda could join the conflict.
The eastern Zaire region also is host to Hutus who fled Rwanda fearing revenge attacks after the 1994 massacre of up to a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

"The war is not limited to Zaire and Rwanda but the whole region," Boutros-Ghali said. "Refugees have left the camps and have spread through the region. Roads have been blocked and we are not able to offer assistance to the refugees."
He said he proposed an international conference as a medium-term solution and that Uganda and Rwanda, who originally had opposed such a meeting, had now agreed to one.

But he said the meeting needed preparation and should include "foreign actors who are playing a role in this tragedy in eastern Zaire." The large quantity of weapons in the region, he said, are "coming from outside," not from Africa.

British Ambassador Sir John Weston told reporters that the situation increased the risk of a further disintegration of an important African nation, namely Zaire, and complicated the already volatile situation in Burundi.

"That's the analysis and I've heard nobody dispute that," he said, adding that nothing had been decided yet in the Security Council. But he said, "We are all clear that the nature of the fighting is accentuated by the fact there are too many arms washing around in the hands of the people who are going at each other."
Weston said the Council was considering four steps:
-- The need for a humanitarian and political emergency plan, put together by Boutros-Ghali and his staff working closely with the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees.
-- An appeal to the Security Council to stop the fighting.
-- A mission to the area, both to focus more sharply on the facts, and perhaps to play a political role.
-- The question of a regional conference.

He said the lead for the conference should come from regional leaders themselves "because we need to be clear on the objectives of any such conference and that it has the full support of the regional players before going beyond an early and preparatory stage."
